image_description: A vintage cream-colored typewriter sits on a wooden surface. The image features a close-up of the keyboard, specifically highlighting the long space bar at the bottom center. In the foreground, loose metal type bars (letters) are scattered on the wood, spelling out fragments like 'I RUM C A RIO'.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated rectangular key spanning the full width of the bottom keyboard row.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The space bar is clearly visible as the longest key in the bottom row, spanning the central width of the keyboard block.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Length is dramatically greater than any other key, roughly ten times the width of a standard letter key.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While longer than adjacent keys, the ratio is approximately 4-5x, not 10x. Typewriter space bars are proportionally shorter than modern PC keyboard space bars.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface is flat or slightly concave.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The key appears to have a slight concave curvature typical of typewriter keys, consistent with the description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Underside connects to a long stabilizer bar mechanism.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The underside and internal mechanical linkage are completely occluded by the keycap itself and the viewing angle.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Label is typically blank with no printed character.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The space bar has no visible letters or symbols printed on its surface.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Positioned centrally between modifier keys on the bottom row.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: It is located in the center of the bottom row, flanked by what appear to be shift/lock mechanisms or edge casing.
The material appears to be black painted metal or hard rubber with a semi-gloss sheen, characteristic of vintage typewriters, rather than modern matte plastic.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Typically white, black, or gray to match keyboard color scheme.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The key is black, contrasting with the cream body, which fits the 'black' option in the taxonomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Part of a standard computer or typewriter keyboard.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The object is clearly part of a manual typewriter keyboard assembly.

artifact_observations.reasoning: The scattered metal type pieces in the foreground show slight deformations and irregular edges. Some characters are difficult to distinguish or appear partially melted into the metal strip, typical of AI generation struggles with small, complex text objects.

The white lettering on the black keys shows slight inconsistency in sharpness and alignment. Some letters appear slightly warped or unevenly raised, lacking the crisp uniformity of real manufactured type.

artifact_observations.location: Top right edge of typewriter body
artifact_observations.reasoning: The edge where the typewriter body meets the background shows slight softness and ambiguity in the boundary, suggesting minor geometric bleeding.

selected_experts.reason: To confirm the specific identification of the space bar within the context of a typewriter vs. computer keyboard.
To rigorously audit the legibility and structural integrity of the letters on the keys and the scattered metal types in the foreground.
To check for edge bleeding between the complex key structures and the typewriter chassis, and to verify the physical separation of the scattered type pieces.
To assess general coherence, lighting consistency, and detect any subtle global artifacts missed by specific auditors.

Physical plausibility of scattered metal type pieces in foreground
Boundary sharpness between keys and chassis
